To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the outcome of fractured shaft of femur depends on the age of the injured, the mechanism of injury, the treatment given and the type of fracture.
the epidemiology of femoral shaft fractures varies according to age and cause, and that the morbidity of the injury depends upon these factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the prevention and treatment of fractured femurs.
the prevention and treatment of these fractures, with particular reference to the outcome.
the epidemiology of femoral shaft fractures, and the effect of this on outcome.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the epidemiology of the fractured femur is important in the assessment of the cause and type of the fracture.
a fractured femur is a complex injury and that its outcome depends on a multitude of factors.
prevention of fractures of the femur is best achieved by the reduction of high-velocity trauma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cause of the injury is more important than the age or type of the patient.
the cause of the injury and its associated factors are as important as the method of treatment in predicting the outcome.
the cause and type of fracture should determine treatment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no one size fits all approach to the management of fractured shafts of the femur.
the cause and mechanism of injury should be considered when deciding on treatment and that the treatment itself may be more important than age in the outcome of these injuries.
